_about: The sources the formal assessment (formal_report.py, formal-assessment.md) rests on: legal status, the provisions used, the exact words, and how each quote was checked. There is NO official EU guideline on detecting AI-written text in research; these are the binding rules on side issues, the soft law on disclosure and responsibility, and the due-process codes. Not legal advice. Re-check a source before relying on it in a dispute: 'checked' says how far each was verified and when.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (General Data Protection Regulation)
sources.checked: once on the source, and the wording matches the published regulation

provisions.quote: not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, which produces legal effects concerning him or her or similarly significantly affects him or her
provisions.use: No decision about a person on a detector score alone: a human reviews every assessment.

provisions.quote: processed lawfully, fairly and in a transparent manner
provisions.use: The person assessed can see what was done and on what basis.

provisions.quote: accurate and, where necessary, kept up to date
provisions.use: Error rates are stated; a wrong finding is corrected.

sources.note: Applies to organisations processing personal data; an opinion about who wrote a text is personal data about its author. No data-protection authority decision on AI-text detectors was found.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act)
sources.checked: once on the source, and the wording matches the published regulation

provisions.quote: marked in a machine-readable format and detectable as artificially generated or manipulated
provisions.use: Binds providers of generative AI, not authors. It is why Claude and ChatGPT text now carries watermarks (see watermarks.md).

provisions.quote: has undergone a process of human review or editorial control
provisions.use: Text under human editorial responsibility is exempt from the public-interest labelling duty: the Act does not oblige a researcher to label a paper or a grant.

provisions.quote: monitoring and detecting prohibited behaviour of students during tests
provisions.use: The high-risk category nearest to detection; by its wording it does not cover manuscripts, grants or reviews (our reading, not an authority's).

sources.note: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI, OJ 24.7.2026) gives systems on the market before 2 August 2026 until 2 December 2026 to comply with Art. 50(2). The Commission's Guidelines on Article 50 (20 July 2026) and the Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-generated Content (10 June 2026) are non-binding.

sources.title: Living guidelines on the responsible use of generative AI in research
sources.body: ERA Forum stakeholders / European Commission, DG Research and Innovation
sources.checked: twice: research pass on the primary document, then an independent text extraction of the same document (2026-11-17)

provisions.quote: These guidelines are non-binding. They complement, but do not replace, applicable legislation and relevant institutional, disciplinary, funder and other requirements.
provisions.use: The specific journal, funder or institution rule comes first.

provisions.quote: AI systems are neither authors nor co-authors nor owners. Authorship implies agency and responsibility, so it lies with researchers.
provisions.use: Responsibility for content stays with the named authors, whatever tool was used.

provisions.quote: Researchers disclose which AI tools or systems were used substantially in their research or reporting processes and describe what they contributed or were used for.
provisions.use: What must be disclosed: substantial use.

provisions.quote: using generative AI as a basic editorial support tool is not a substantial use
provisions.use: Language polishing is not a breach.

provisions.quote: spellchecking, grammar correction, polishing or formatting, generally do not need to be disclosed. In case of doubt, disclosure is advised.
provisions.use: The alternative proposition (human text, AI-polished) is legitimate conduct.

provisions.quote: Ensure that the judgement task is not delegated to an AI tool when assessing scientific quality and merit of proposals and papers.
provisions.use: What a reviewer may not do.

provisions.quote: do not disclose unpublished proposals, manuscripts, review reports or key ideas through non-secured AI tools, including through excerpts or prompts
provisions.use: The confidentiality gate: confidential text is never sent to web detectors.

provisions.quote: researchers can disclose the use of generative AI transparently and without concerns of being disadvantaged
provisions.use: Disclosed use must not be held against anyone.

provisions.quote: content may contain hidden prompts or invisible instructions intended to influence generative AI tools
provisions.use: Hidden-prompt checks are an expected safeguard.

sources.note: The words 'detect', 'detection' and 'detector' do not appear anywhere in the document: it gives no detection or sanction procedure.

sources.title: The European Code of Conduct for Research Integrity, Revised Edition 2023
sources.status: professional code; the reference integrity standard in Horizon Europe grant agreements
sources.checked: twice: research pass on the primary document, then an independent text extraction of the same document (2026-11-17)

provisions.quote: disclose the use of AI and automated tools
provisions.use: Reviewers and editors disclose their own AI use.

provisions.quote: Hiding the use of AI or automated tools in the creation of content or drafting of publications.
provisions.use: Listed among unacceptable practices: the conduct this assessment is about.

provisions.quote: Accusing a researcher of misconduct or other violations in a malicious way.
provisions.use: Also an unacceptable practice: an unfounded accusation is itself a violation.

provisions.quote: Anyone accused of research misconduct is presumed innocent until proven otherwise.
provisions.use: The assessment reports evidence; it does not find anyone guilty.

provisions.quote: Investigations are conducted confidentially in order to protect those involved.
provisions.use: The assessment and the case label stay confidential.

provisions.quote: Persons accused of research misconduct are given full details of the allegation(s) and are allowed a fair process for responding to allegations and presenting evidence.
provisions.use: The author sees all the evidence and can answer before anything is concluded.

provisions.quote: proportionate to the severity of the violation
provisions.use: Any consequence is for the competent body to weigh.

provisions.quote: Appropriate restorative action is taken when researchers are exonerated of an allegation of misconduct.
provisions.use: If the concern does not hold, it is withdrawn explicitly.

sources.title: ENFSI Guideline for Evaluative Reporting in Forensic Science, v3.0
sources.body: European Network of Forensic Science Institutes
sources.checked: once on the source, and the wording matches the published regulation

provisions.quote: Balance, Logic, Robustness and Transparency
provisions.use: The four requirements this assessment's wording follows.

provisions.quote: at least one pair of propositions
provisions.use: Evidence is always weighed under two stated propositions, never one.

sources.note: Evaluative reports state how much more probable the findings are under one proposition than under the other (a likelihood ratio), never the probability that a proposition is true ('transposing the conditional').

sources.title: Horizon Europe standard application form (RIA, IA), Part B: guidance on the use of generative AI tools for the preparation of the proposal
sources.status: call condition for Horizon Europe applicants
sources.checked: twice: research pass on the primary document, then an independent text extraction of the same document (2026-11-17)

provisions.quote: Applicants are fully responsible for the content of the proposal (even those parts produced by the AI tool) and must be transparent in disclosing which AI tools were used and how they were utilized.
provisions.use: What a Horizon Europe applicant owes: responsibility and disclosure.

sources.title: Horizon Europe proposal evaluation: standard briefing for experts, version 13.0
sources.status: Commission instructions to expert evaluators (read on a university copy)
sources.checked: twice: research pass on the primary document, then an independent text extraction of the same document (2026-11-17)

provisions.ref: Use of generative AI for proposal preparation
provisions.quote: The use of generative AI tools in drafting proposals may not be considered by expert evaluators as a reason to penalise a proposal.
provisions.use: AI use in a proposal is not in itself a ground for a lower score; quality and accuracy are.

provisions.ref: Use of generative AI tools for proposal evaluation
provisions.quote: must not delegate the evaluation of proposals to AI tools
provisions.use: What an evaluator may not do.

provisions.quote: the use of generative AI tools for evaluation, particularly generative AI online tools, may represent a breach of the confidentiality requirements of your contract
provisions.use: Why proposals under evaluation are never sent to web detectors.

sources.title: The use of AI in grant proposal evaluation: guidelines for ERC panel members and remote reviewers
sources.checked: once: read on the source given, by the research pass (2026-11-17)

provisions.quote: upload a proposal, or part of it, to an online AI tool
provisions.use: Not allowed for ERC reviewers.

provisions.quote: a delegation of the evaluation task
provisions.use: How the ERC classes generating a draft review with AI.

sources.title: Authorship and AI tools (COPE position statement)
sources.checked: once: read on the source given, by the research pass (2026-11-17)

provisions.quote: must be transparent in disclosing
provisions.use: Authors disclose how an AI tool was used and remain responsible for all content.

sources.title: Suspected AI-generated manuscripts (COPE case 26-11, Council advice)
sources.status: publishing-ethics advice on a case (not formal guidance)
sources.checked: once: read on the source given, by the research pass (2026-11-17)

provisions.quote: the first steps should be to contact the authors in a neutral tone
provisions.use: The first step after an assessment is a neutral question, not an accusation.

sources.title: When editors suspect AI (COPE Forum topic discussion)
sources.checked: once: read on the source given, by the research pass (2026-11-17)

provisions.quote: Current tools are not perfect and editors should not cite suspected AI use as a reason for rejection if they cannot prove it.
provisions.use: A detector result alone is not a ground for action.

sources.title: ICMJE Recommendations, section on artificial intelligence
sources.body: International Committee of Medical Journal Editors
sources.status: journal-editor standard followed by most medical journals
sources.checked: once: read on the source given, by the research pass (2026-11-17)

provisions.quote: Nondisclosure of AI use may require corrective action and may be construed as misconduct in some circumstances.
provisions.use: The possible consequence of non-disclosure, decided by the journal.

sources.title: Casework note: complaints relating to AI and academic misconduct
sources.body: Office of the Independent Adjudicator for Higher Education (England and Wales)
sources.status: ombudsman casework (students; persuasive by analogy, not EU)
sources.checked: once: read on the source given, by the research pass (2026-11-17)

provisions.quote: The responsibility is on the provider to prove
provisions.use: The burden is on whoever alleges.

provisions.quote: on the balance of probability
provisions.use: The standard of proof used there.

sources.note: In case CS072504 (partly justified) the provider had not considered whether the detector might be less reliable for non-native English speakers.

sources.title: Understanding false positives within our AI writing detection capabilities
sources.checked: once: read on the source given, by the research pass (2026-11-17)

provisions.quote: Turnitin does not make a determination of misconduct
provisions.use: Even the best-known vendor says its score is not a finding.
